fix: transcoding actually respects selected quality tier.
fix: i18n strings now load in the correct Jellyfin UI language (de, us, es, fr, nl, zh-cn)

Fix queue panel resetting progress bar when new items are added

Incremental DOM updates replace full re-renders so the active download's
progress bar is preserved when a second item joins the queue.

Add multi-download queue

Downloads now enqueue instead of starting immediately. Each queued item has its own cancel button; cancelling removes only that item and the next starts automatically. The bottom-right panel shows all queued items with live progress for the active one. Queue is in-memory only.
Update logo, rename console prefix to [TranscodeDownloader], fix README and manifest

Fix transcode quality tiers and stale item on first page load

- On first load, quality sheet now awaits metadata before building the
  tier list, so only valid bitrates (below source bitrate) are shown
- Quality sheet now re-derives the item ID from the URL at open time,
  preventing downloads targeting the previous movie when navigating
  between items before the hash-change event fires

Replace dropdown button with action sheet menu entry

- Remove injected select+button from the detail page
- Add 'Download (Transcode…)' entry to Jellyfin's native 'Mehr' menu
- Quality selection via a second overlay in Jellyfin's action sheet style
- Fixes reload-required bug; no longer disrupts the detail page layout

fix: show plugin logo in catalog and installed plugin detail page

- Add imageUrl to manifest.json so the catalog displays the logo
- Include logo.png in the release zip for the installed plugin detail page

rename: QuickDownload → Transcode Downloader + add logo and build CI

- Plugin display name is now "Transcode Downloader"
- All internals renamed to Jellyfin.Plugin.TranscodeDownloader
- Controller route changed to /TranscodeDownloader/ClientScript
- Added logo.png
- Added PR build workflow

Fix: force transcode to honour selected quality tier

Without allowVideoStreamCopy=false Jellyfin could direct-stream the
original file, ignoring MaxStreamingBitrate and MaxHeight entirely.
Downloads now correctly re-encode to the selected resolution and bitrate.

Fix: force transcode to honour selected quality tier

Without allowVideoStreamCopy=false Jellyfin could direct-stream the
original file, ignoring MaxStreamingBitrate and MaxHeight entirely.
Downloads now correctly re-encode to the selected resolution and bitrate.
fix: delay revokeObjectURL to prevent download failure after completion

fix: button appears on first load without page reload

Replace 20x250ms polling retry loop with a MutationObserver that fires
the moment Jellyfin's SPA renders the detail-view container. The old
loop could time out before the SPA finished hydrating, requiring a
manual page reload to see the download button.

fix: use ApiClient.getItem() for metadata fetch to avoid 401

Jellyfin 10.11 rejects api_key query-param auth on the Items endpoint,
causing the dropdown to stay empty. Switch to client.getItem() which
sends the correct Authorization header.

fix: populate dropdown after UI injection to eliminate race condition

The metadata fetch often completed before Jellyfin rendered the detail
container, so populateDropdown() exited early (select === null) without
ever setting currentItem. Clicking Download then silently did nothing.

- Move currentItem assignment before the early return in populateDropdown()
- Re-call populateDropdown() after injecting the UI if data already arrived
- Reset currentItem when navigating to a new item to avoid stale options

fix: strip Accept-Encoding/Content-Encoding to prevent compressed-body corruption

Jellyfin's static file middleware serves index.html pre-compressed when the
client advertises Accept-Encoding. The IStartupFilter middleware was buffering
those compressed bytes and writing them back with Content-Encoding: gzip still
set, causing browsers to report 'cannot decode raw data'.

Fix: remove Accept-Encoding from the request before intercepting so upstream
never activates compression; also strip Content-Encoding from the response.

fix: inject script tag via middleware — button now appears without companion plugins

The script tag is now injected by an ASP.NET Core IStartupFilter that
intercepts index.html responses in Jellyfin's HTTP pipeline. No File
Transformation plugin required, no disk writes, no timing sensitivity.

Also fixes plugin loading error in the admin UI (Plugin constructor now
calls SetAttributes).

fix: call SetAttributes in Plugin constructor so CanUninstall doesn't throw

BasePlugin (non-generic) never calls SetAttributes — only BasePlugin<T> does
in its own constructor. Without it, AssemblyFilePath stays null, and
CanUninstall throws NullReferenceException when GET /Plugins serializes the
plugin list, breaking the admin plugins page on every page load.

Fix: inject IApplicationPaths and call SetAttributes the same way BasePlugin<T>
does, giving Jellyfin a valid assembly path and data folder path.

Serve client script from controller and inject in-memory

- QuickDownloadController serves the embedded plugin.js at GET /QuickDownload/ClientScript (AllowAnonymous) so the web root never needs to be writable
- WebAssetInjector registers an in-memory File Transformation callback instead of patching index.html on disk; survives Jellyfin web updates and is auto-removed on plugin uninstall
- On-disk fallback retained for installs without File Transformation, with a loud actionable log recommending FT >= v2.2.1.0
- Base-path-aware script src for Jellyfin deployments behind a sub-path

name: JellyFlare [✓]
overview: Customisable announcement banners for Jellyfin.

Display announcement banners at the top of the Jellyfin web UI. Set up rotating messages or a permanent notice with per-entry colours, flexible scheduling, dismiss controls and link support. All configured from the Jellyfin admin dashboard.  
  
Universal Repo 
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorganKryze/jellyflare/main/manifest.json

versions.changelog:
- Fix the banner covering the top navigation on Jellyfin 12.0's new "modern" UI. JellyFlare now detects the layout and pushes the nav bar and content down instead of drawing over them. 10.11 and TV unchanged. (fixes #12)

**Jellyfin 12.0:** you don't need the File Transformation plugin. JavaScript Injector injects the banner on its own. If you kept File Transformation from 10.11, remove it: its current build isn't 12.0-compatible and, while installed, stops the banner from injecting.

Thanks to @nothing2obvi for the report and for confirming the File Transformation behaviour on 12.0. ❤️

- Add per-banner link popup hint: each rotation message and permanent entry can now carry its own optional hint text shown above the Open/Copy/Cancel buttons, overriding the global default. Per-banner hint → global default → nothing (when both empty). Existing setups keep working unchanged. The Settings-tab field is relabeled "Default link popup hint" to reflect the fallback (requested by @nerdc0re-net #9)

- Fix maintenance mode error 500 on Jellyfin 10.11.10: `IUserManager.Users` was removed and replaced by `GetUsers()`; the plugin now compiles against the 10.11.10 SDK so the call resolves correctly (thanks @LRoffic for the report — #11)
- Bump minimum supported Jellyfin version to 10.11.10 (users on 10.11.6-10.11.9 could stay on v1.15.1 until they update Jellyfin)

- Fix banner not showing on Jellyfin instances configured with a base URL (e.g. `/jellyfin`); plugin fetches now go through `ApiClient.getUrl()` so the base URL is honored (thanks @Kayoku and @FazeThree71 for the report — #10)
- Add Monthly schedule type for banners: target the nth weekday of every month (e.g. "second Tuesday", "last Friday"), with an optional time window

- Add per-user banner muting: users can hide the rotating and/or permanent banner for their own account from their Jellyfin Display settings
- Per-account preference syncs across devices and live across open tabs; maintenance mode is never affected
- Add admin master switch to allow/forbid user muting, plus a configurable warning text (Settings tab)

- Add limit on link preview size
- Add option for comment on link popup

- Fix copy and open link in Jellyfin Media Player on desktop not working
- Update CI to avoid overwriting releases

- Add route filtering on each banner
- Add new project status in the README: project stays active but has reach a satisfying state and stays opens to bug report and feature requests but will not be as proactive as in its early development

- Add scheduling for maintenance mode and restart
- Improve UX for maintenance tab
- Add documentation link to the config page
- Add dependency warning on the config page as a warning banner

- (Tested, but use it with caution) Add a maintenance tab to let you work on your instance without user connecting to the server
- Add preview of affected users (maintenance)
- Add a reset button (maintenance) and link it to the global reset button
- Adjust dismiss button font sizes based on config settings
- Fixed close button visibility logic based on config

- Fixed the "hide all" configuration not being effective
- Added issue templates

Important changes:

- Update manifest description
- Add refresh prompt on each save
- Improve reset mechanism clarity with three distinct buttons and updated labels alongside alerts to save the config
- Improve alert rendering on misconfiguration on input validation
- Regroup isolated settings into Behavior category
- Dismissing a message, all messages, or the permanent banner now syncs instantly to other open tabs via a BroadcastChannel.
- Remove or update legacy code from first implementation

Various refactoring, safety and robustness fixes detailed below:

- `TextAlign` and `TransitionSpeed` are now whitelisted on save; invalid values normalise to `"center"` / `"normal"` rather than being stored verbatim.
- `parseInt` calls in `checkTimeWindow` now always pass radix `10`, preventing silent misparses on malformed time strings.
- Invalid-date checks for fixed schedules use `isNaN(date.getTime())` instead of `isNaN(date)` for clarity.
- `closeBtn.innerHTML` replaced with `closeBtn.textContent` for consistency with the rest of the codebase.
- Token retrieval deduplicated into a single `getToken()` helper used at both call sites.
- French tooltip text on the close and dismiss-all buttons replaced with English equivalents.
- Fixed a 50 ms race where the rotation timer could fire `tick()` before the navigation debounce resolved. The timer is now cleared immediately at the top of `onNavigate()` when `showInDashboard` is `false`.
- Plugin startup now gives up after a fixed retry count instead of looping indefinitely.
- Save endpoint rejects dangerous URL schemes (`javascript:` etc.) in both rotation and permanent entries.
- Save endpoint validates schedule types and returns a clear error for unknown values instead of silently defaulting to "always".
- Numeric settings (durations, banner height, active index) are clamped to their allowed ranges on save.
- Config changes are picked up on the next page navigation instead of waiting for the old rotation queue to finish.
- Layout recalculation now batches all reads before all writes, avoiding repeated forced reflows.
- Resize observer on the header is re-attached on every banner show, preventing stale references from rapid hide/show cycles.
- Rotation-message and permanent-entry row builders (~460 lines of duplicated code) replaced with a single shared factory function.
- Default presets, rotation messages, and permanent entries consolidated into one `CONFIG_DEFAULTS` object.
- Each Settings subsection (Appearance, Timing, Controls, Behaviour, Presets) has its own reset function; Reset and Wipe buttons delegate to these.
- Row-field collection extracted into a single shared helper used by both collect functions.
- Default text colour normalised to `#ffffff` in the data model for both rotation and permanent entries.
- Magic numbers in the banner script replaced with named constants (`BANNER_Z_INDEX`, `POPUP_Z_INDEX`, `MOBILE_BREAKPOINT`, etc.).
- Add drag and drop feature to messages collections
- Permanent banner can now optionally be dismissed, persistence behavior can be configured
- The app now tries to open link outside the in-app web browser framework, but for unsupported platform also let the user copy the url (better transparency)

- Fixed banner animation hiding first carousel arrows and title
- Added new default rotation entry
- Banner in dashboard visibility defaults to false and is set at the bottom of the config page
- Normalise line endings to inside jq before the value touches the shell

- Improved admin dashboard detection, add warning for the visibility option
- Fixed XSS vector: banner link URLs are now validated against an allowlist (https://, http://, /); any other scheme including javascript: is silently rejected
- Fixed privilege escalation: the config save endpoint (POST /JellyFlare/config) now requires admin-level credentials (RequiresElevation policy); standard user tokens are rejected
- Config and script endpoints now require authentication; unauthenticated visitors receive no banner and cannot read plugin configuration: the plugin is intended for registered users only, consistent with JS Injector
- CI actions pinned to full commit SHAs to eliminate supply-chain risk from re-tagged upstream actions
- change permanent docs image.

- add configurable sizes for dismiss buttons in settings;
- add option to show banner in admin dashboard.

- permanent banner can be disabled but still saved;
- add customization to hide all button and close button.
- add quick access to the plugin from the dashboard sidebar
- first version, may be unstable

versions.changelog: Fixes for 1.8.0, almost all reported by users of it. JELLYFIN 12.1: StarTrack appears in the new Material-UI top bar - 12.1 moved navigation there and the nav drawer the My Ratings link used is not in that layout (#27). FIXES: opening a film from My Ratings no longer freezes page scrolling (six code paths closed the overlay and only one released the scroll lock, leaving the whole web UI unscrollable until a reload) (#27); Back closes My Ratings instead of navigating the page behind it (#27); half stars are cut at the middle of the glyph again (#27); 'out of ten' now applies to your own ratings too, not only community averages - panel, recent list, cards, diary and comparison (#27); Letterboxd 'Verify login' opens its session the way a real push does - it never used FlareSolverr, so a correct server still failed it, and a stale pasted cookie was used forever and never questioned, which is worse than none - it now retries without your cookies and on a fresh challenge and says what actually fixes a Cloudflare block (#24); the self-check no longer reports a failure for a read-only index.html, the normal state in Docker, on a server that is injecting perfectly well by its other route (#20); a duplicate copy of a film in the library no longer collects a second rating on import. NEW: StarTrack tells you when your browser is running a cached old copy of it, with a Reload button, and never reloads on its own (#20); a My Ratings button in the rating panel (#28); remove from watchlist directly from the watchlist (#28).

Jellyfin 12 support from one codebase: two builds, 1.8.0.0 for 10.11 and 1.8.0.1 for 12; the catalogue picks the right one. LETTERBOXD: 'Sync everything' imports your whole profile live - every rating including films rated but never logged, every dated diary entry, then watchlist, likes and Top 4 - with never-logged films placed in the order you rated them; watchlist sync works again (Letterboxd removed the RSS feed, the page is read instead); likes, Top 4 and sign-in get through Cloudflare via an optional FlareSolverr, and back off politely with a visible note without one; imports never overwrite reviews or dates they do not carry; a known year is a matching constraint (Fall 2022 is not The Fall 2006); duplicate library copies rate the one you already rated; likes are dated by the viewing, not the import. DIARY: one viewing, one row - a playback row and its later rating merge (timezone-safe); pre-rolls and trailers under two minutes are not logged; a rating from any source fills an unrated row. RATINGS: admin choice of stars, stars+/10, or /10 everywhere an average shows (display only); IMDb ratings CSV import, auto-detected; IMDb/Yamtrack export reports what it left out. SIMKL: pull converges (#19) - any shared id matches. FIXES: tick boxes hidden by global CSS themes; poster badges fetched in one batch instead of one request per card; settings-load failures say so instead of showing everything unticked. NEW: 'Is StarTrack working?' self-check with a paste-ready report. Everything translated in all 8 languages.

name: Bonfire [✓]
description:
Adds multi-user profile switching to Jellyfin. A single account can have up to five isolated profiles — each with its own watch history, parental controls, and library access.  
  
Universal Repo 
Source: https://ahouseofbards.github.io/Bonfire-JellyProfiles/manifest.json  
Github: https://github.com/AHouseOfBards/Bonfire-JellyProfiles
overview: Multi-user profile switching for Jellyfin.

versions.changelog:
**Fixed**

- On 2019 LG TVs (webOS 4.5), Bonfire did not start at all. [#34]
- With "Ask who's watching on startup" off, there was no Switch Profile button and no way to switch.
- After signing out of the iOS app, the previous account's profile stayed on the sign-in screen and carried over to the next account.
- On iPad, your own profiles could appear as a linked Bonfire, and Manage Profiles asked you to open yourself first.
- The profile picture in the header was drawn zoomed in and blurry.

**Fixed**

- Security: any account could run script in an administrator's browser through the Bonfire settings page. Please update.
- Security: a PIN typed into a TV or app sign-in screen could be guessed with no limit.
- Security: someone using a profile in a browser could take over the main account behind it.
- On Android TV, Roku and other TV apps, choosing a profile and entering its PIN was refused.
- A profile limited to one TV could be missing from that TV's sign-in screen.
- Skipping Quick Connect on known TVs also removed it for other people with the same TV model.
- Signing in on a TV could occasionally fail with a server error.
- Creating a profile could fail with "The supplied value is invalid". [#33]
- The profile picker ran off the bottom of the screen on a TV. [#31]
- A profile kept its old rating after its account's rating was lowered.
- Clearing your PIN, or using the emergency disable code, could stop your password working.
- An account with a PIN could not change its Jellyfin password.
- Creating two profiles at once could go over the profile limit.
- The Signed-in devices list in the dashboard could fail to load.
- The create form showed only four libraries at a time.

**Changed**

- A profile keeps every restriction set on its account, such as remote access, schedules and bitrate.
- Profiles in another household's Bonfire need a PIN, unless their owner allows switching on the home network.
- Hidden Bonfire profiles can no longer be opened.
- Removing someone from your Bonfire changes its code, so they cannot rejoin with the old one.
- Reopening the app keeps the profile you were using. Going back to your main profile asks for its PIN.
- Manage Profiles needs your main profile open.

**Added**

- Thirty starter avatars to pick from, on by default. Turn them off in Dashboard -> Bonfire -> Avatar Library. [#32]
- Picture quality for profile pictures and avatars: Dashboard -> Bonfire -> Picture quality.
- A New code button for your Bonfire.
- A loader for the Samsung Tizen app, so Bonfire updates reach the TV without rebuilding the app. [#16]

**Fixed**

- Giving a profile a new library in Dashboard -> Users was undone the next time anyone entered that profile. Grants made there are now kept. To take a library away from a profile, edit the profile. [#30]
- Turning on "Skip Quick Connect on known devices" took Quick Connect away from apps that already have a password screen. It now applies only to Android TV, which is the one that needs it.

**Added**

- Profiles can appear on the sign-in screens of Jellyfin for Roku, Swiftfin, Findroid and Wholphin, the same as Android TV. Turn off automatic sign in on the app, or it goes straight into the last account.
- Apps that have no user list of their own can enter a profile by typing the profile's name and its PIN.

**Changed**

- The README is shorter. Library artwork, Bonfire sharing and known limitations now have their own pages under docs/.

**Added**

- Profiles can now appear on the sign-in screen of apps that never load the web client, such as Android TV, and be opened with their PIN. New settings under Dashboard -> Bonfire -> TVs & Apps, all off until you turn them on.
- On those screens a profile shows the name you gave it, not the full account name.
- An account that owns profiles can sign in with its PIN as well as its password.
- Apps can be sent straight to the password field instead of a Quick Connect code.
- "Who's watching?" on startup can be set per device instead of everywhere at once.

**Works on Jellyfin 12.0.** The same build serves 10.11 and 12.0 — there is nothing extra to install.

**Fixed**

- On Jellyfin 12.0 the Switch Profile button was missing from the header. Its default layout keeps the old header in the page but hides it, and Bonfire was adding the button there.
- In the profile form, text boxes would not take a click and dropdowns would not open — the page jumped to the top instead. Jellyfin's account menu was being left open, and its focus handling and Bonfire's fought each other.
- The Switch Profile button could appear beside the wrong icon at the wrong size, then move a second or two later. It now appears once, beside your account icon.
- Importing avatars from a folder failed on Jellyfin 12.0, and on any server where an administrator had turned legacy authorization off.
- The Bonfire section on your profile page sat against the left edge while the rest of the page was centred.
- The rename and merge buttons in the device list were unstyled, and drew as empty boxes on televisions without an emoji font.

**Changed**

- Bonfire follows your theme's accent colour on Jellyfin 12.0, which publishes that colour under a new name.

**Fixed**

- Switching to someone's main profile wiped that person's library access, and their sub-profiles' access with it. If this has happened to you, re-tick their libraries in Jellyfin's user settings after updating. [#27]
- Switching into an administrator's account quietly removed their admin rights and hid them from the login screen. [#27]
- Restricting a profile to specific devices could lock it out of every device, including the ones you picked. [#16]
- On a TV, picking a profile changed the name at the top but left you in your main account — same libraries, same Continue Watching, same Next Up. [#16]
- On a TV, moving off the first profile jumped straight to Manage Profiles and no other profile could be reached. [#16]
- On a TV the profile cards had no size and the focus outline never appeared, so nothing looked selectable. Save could also sit below the bottom of the profile form with no way to reach it on a remote. [#16]
- The profile switcher said you were signed in as your main profile even while a sub-profile was in use.
- A profile, device or Bonfire group you had just saved could silently not be there.
- Anything added while the plugin's settings page was open was undone when an administrator pressed Save.
- One computer could appear several times in the device list, and devices that sent no name all read as "Unknown Device".
- Forgetting a profile's only allowed device silently made that profile available everywhere. It is refused now, and says which profiles are in the way.
- "Try again in 15 minutes" after too many wrong PINs. It now tells you the wait it is actually enforcing, which is usually far less.
- Device "last seen" dates reset every time Jellyfin restarted, and the device list never dropped hardware nobody uses any more.
- A language could stop loading until Jellyfin was restarted, dropping everyone back to English.
- Switching profiles on a light theme flashed a black screen, and a switch that went wrong left the screen blank for four seconds.
- The profile screen re-downloaded every profile picture on every page load. Your browser keeps them now.

**Added**

- Bonfire knows when it is on a television, and makes the profile pictures, text and focus outline large enough to use from across a room.
- Rename a device, or tell Bonfire that two entries are the same machine. "Tidy up duplicates" folds together the several devices one browser makes — a profile allowed on any of them stays allowed.
- A list of everyone signed in, with the household each profile belongs to, and a way to sign one device out.
- Export and import the plugin's configuration, so there is a copy of your profiles and PINs somewhere other than one file.
- The audit log can be filtered by name and date, and downloaded.
- Polish, contributed by danis101. [#26]
- TROUBLESHOOTING.md, which answers the most common report first: Bonfire does not edit index.html by default, so a file with no plugin tags in it is a healthy install.

**Changed**

- The Switch Profile button now sits next to your account icon in the header, instead of at the end of the row.
- The interface reads correctly on light Jellyfin themes, where separators and muted text used to be invisible.
- Bonfire does far less work in the background — most noticeable on a TV, and it steps back further while something is playing.
- The "restart to finish updating" notice now names the version running and the version waiting, so you can tell whether your restart worked. [#25]

**New**

- Bonfire no longer edits Jellyfin's `index.html`. The client script is added to the page as it is served, so there is nothing to re-apply after a Jellyfin update and no file permissions to grant. Patching the file stays available as a legacy option under **Advanced → Client script**. (#17, #11, #3)
- The switcher follows your theme's accent colour instead of always drawing Jellyfin blue.
- Profile screens use the whole window on a desktop instead of one phone-width column.
- The picker shows which profile you are currently watching as.

**Fixed**

- On Android, picking a profile could bring the picker straight back, over and over, and a PIN-protected profile could drop you at the account login.
- Picking a profile showed nothing at all for the second or two it takes, so the tap read as missed. The profile you picked now shows a spinner, and the screen no longer goes black while it loads.
- Opening a profile took several seconds and could drop you back on a screen you had already left.
- Bonfire rewrote `index.html` on startup even when set never to touch it.
- The settings page reported the client script as installed whenever the plugin was loaded at all, including on servers where nothing was reaching the page.
- Add Profile was missing from the Manage Profiles screen.
- Library names were cut off to "3D Movi…" when choosing artwork.
- **Upload avatars** and **Upload a folder** were unstyled text instead of buttons.
- "PIN Protected" showed in red and "No PIN" in green — the wrong way round.
- The audit log ran the time into the address as "12:09:28 PMIP".

**Changed**

- The plugin is called **Bonfire** in the Jellyfin sidebar.
- Plugin settings are split into tabs — General, Avatars, Accounts, Activity and Advanced — instead of one page five screens tall.
- Switcher Style and Your Bonfire move out of the profile grid into their own **Settings** screen. Bonfire Grouping is now called Your Bonfire.
- Add Profile appears on Manage Profiles only. The "Who's watching?" screen is people to pick from.
- Setting a profile picture is one panel rather than six controls. The paste-a-URL box is gone: a linked picture could not be cropped, was never stored on your server, and disappeared without warning when the link died.
- Libraries and their artwork are one list, with the artwork controls behind a switch.
- Delete is no longer as prominent as Save.

**New**

- Library artwork can be set per profile. Jellyfin builds a library tile from the items inside it, so a Kids profile could see a poster from a film it cannot open; each profile can now be given its own picture for a library, or none at all. (#19)
- Administrators can set the switcher defaults for the whole server, under Dashboard → Plugins → Bonfire. Anyone who has already chosen keeps their own setting. (#14)
- Avatars can be uploaded several at a time, or a whole folder at once. Administrators with a prepared set already on the server can point at its folder and import it. (#14)
- The profile picker has a Cancel button when you opened it yourself, so you can go back to what you were watching.

**Fixed**

- Switching a profile failed with "Invalid username or password" on Jellyfin 10.11.11, and signed the master account out. (#15)
- On Samsung Tizen, picking a profile changed the avatar but left you in the original account. (#15, #16)
- On a TV, the remote could steer the Jellyfin page hidden behind the Bonfire screen. (#16)
- The TV Back button raised Samsung’s "exit application?" prompt behind the Bonfire screen. Back now steps back one screen instead. (#15)
- "Switch Profile" now appears on the Settings page, not only in the header dropdown. (#14)
- Profile pictures could be zoomed but not dragged.
- Save and Cancel are scrolled into view when a remote reaches them, so long profile forms no longer look frozen. (#15)
- Pictures now load in clients that bundle their own web client, such as Samsung Tizen.
- A missing script tag in index.html now says which of the three causes it is. (#17)

**Changed**

- The emergency disable link appears only once an administrator has set a code.
- Error messages, hints and warnings cut down throughout.

First stable release of the 1.3 line, consolidating the 1.2.x pre-releases. ■ NEW — Tag-based content filtering. Each sub-profile can block or allow content by Jellyfin tag (for example "adults", "teens", "kids"), alongside the existing parental rating limit. Tags are inherited, so tagging a series or a whole library applies to everything inside it, and enforcement happens server-side — meaning it holds on every client, including ones that cannot show the profile switcher at all. Blocked tags are additive with the master account's, and an allow-list can only narrow the master's, so a sub-profile can never see more than its parent. ■ NEW — Reorganised profile editor. Creating and editing a profile is now grouped into four titled sections: Profile (name, colour, picture), Security (PIN, LAN bypass, auto-lock), Libraries, and Content & Device Restrictions. Previously every field sat in one flat list in the order features had been added. Sections are plain blocks rather than collapsible panels so D-pad focus order on TV stays predictable, and the layout adapts to phone widths. ■ NEW — The settings page now lists master accounts with their sub-profiles nested underneath, instead of two separate tables. ■ SECURITY — Fixed a stored cross-site scripting flaw in profile avatar images and colours. Because Bonfire groups render profiles from linked households on each other's switcher screens, a crafted value could run script in another user's browser and steal their session token. Values are now validated on the server and escaped on render. ■ SECURITY — Profile PINs are now stored as salted PBKDF2-SHA256 hashes rather than unsalted SHA-256, under which a 4-8 digit PIN was recoverable almost instantly from the configuration file. Existing PINs keep working and are upgraded automatically the next time they are entered. ■ SECURITY — An account with no PIN can no longer be switched into from a shared Bonfire, and the local-network PIN bypass no longer applies when stepping into another household's account. Also removed an open redirect on the profile image endpoint. ■ FIX — The dashboard's client-script warnings are now accurate. They re-check index.html on every page load rather than reporting server-startup state, a "Re-check Now" button re-runs the injection without a Jellyfin restart, and the message names the specific cause — including whether Jellyfin can write the file at all. The advisory notice can be dismissed on installs where the file is not writable without elevating. ■ FIX — Permission-fix commands are generated for the account Jellyfin actually runs as, rather than covering every possibility at once. ■ FIX — Editing a profile no longer erases device whitelist entries for devices that are switched off, and the device picker is correctly scoped to your own household. ■ FIX — A saved PIN no longer displays as "No PIN" on your own network, and profile changes appear immediately instead of requiring a page reload. ■ PERFORMANCE — Profile switching no longer rewrites the entire audit log on the request, the client script is served with revalidation so browsers pick up updates on their own, and a listener leak that made the interface progressively less responsive over a session has been fixed.

⚠️ BETA RELEASE — not a finished release; please report issues on GitHub. ▸ Settings page: master accounts and sub-profiles were listed as two separate tables, so working out which profiles belonged to which account meant reading the "Master Account" column on every row. There is now a single list of master accounts, each with its sub-profiles collapsed underneath it behind a "2 sub-profiles" toggle. PIN status and Reset PIN are available at both levels as before. Any sub-profile whose master account no longer exists — normally the residue of a partially failed deletion — is listed separately under "Unlinked sub-profiles" rather than disappearing, so it can still be found and managed. ▸ The permission-fix commands are now generated for the account Jellyfin is actually running as, and the page states which account that is. Previously they had to cover every possibility at once: on Windows, Jellyfin runs either as a service (NT AUTHORITY\NetworkService) or as the signed-in user when installed as a tray/desktop app, so the icacls command granted Modify to ALL local users in order to work in both cases. It now grants access to exactly one account — the real one — which is both less to type and a considerably narrower permission on a file inside Program Files. ▸ The same applies to the Linux and Docker chown commands, which previously assumed the service account was named "jellyfin". That is the convention but not a guarantee, and the commands silently did nothing useful when it was not. If the account cannot be determined, the page falls back to the previous broader commands, so nothing is lost on unusual setups.

New: Tag-based content filtering for sub-profiles. Each profile can now block or allow content by Jellyfin tag (e.g. 'adults', 'teens', 'kids'), matching Jellyfin's own parental-control tag feature. Tags are inherited, so tagging a series or an entire library applies to everything inside it, and enforcement is server-side so it holds on every client. Blocked tags are additive with the master account's and an allow-list can only narrow the master's, so a sub-profile can never see more than its parent. Security: fixed a stored XSS in profile avatar images and colours — these are rendered on other households' switcher screens via Bonfire groups, so a crafted value could steal another user's session token; values are now validated server-side and escaped on render. Security: profile PINs are now stored as salted PBKDF2-SHA256 hashes instead of unsalted SHA-256 (a 4-8 digit PIN was trivially recoverable from the config file); existing PINs keep working and upgrade automatically on next entry. Security: an account with no PIN can no longer be switched into from a shared Bonfire, and the LAN PIN bypass no longer applies across accounts. Security: removed an open redirect on the profile image endpoint. Fix: the client-script injection now verifies the script is actually present before reporting success — previously an index.html without the expected anchors reported success while the switcher silently never loaded, and the dashboard's failure banner could never appear. Fix: index.html is now written atomically so an interrupted write cannot corrupt the Jellyfin web client. Fix: audit log entries no longer reverse order when trimmed.

Fix: Plugin now loads correctly on Jellyfin 10.11.5. The previous release was compiled against 10.11.6, which caused a loader-level assembly version mismatch (FileNotFoundException on MediaBrowser.Common/Controller/Model) on servers running 10.11.5. Compile target downgraded to 10.11.5 — the plugin remains fully compatible with 10.11.6 and later patch releases.
Release 1.1.0: Codebase cleanup, optimization, documentation updates, and developer API reference alignment.
Initial release.

versions.changelog:
## ✨ New Features

- **Notify chosen users**: tick non-admin users on the new **Settings** tab to show them the badge too.
- **Counts only**: they see how many plugins changed, and can't dismiss or restart.

## 🎨 Improvements

- **Tabbed plugin page**: the page is split into **Updates** and **Settings** tabs.

## ✨ New Features

- **Notify chosen users**: tick non-admin users on the new **Settings** tab to show them the badge too.
- **Counts only**: they see how many plugins changed, and can't dismiss or restart.

## 🎨 Improvements

- **Tabbed plugin page**: the page is split into **Updates** and **Settings** tabs.

## ✨ New Features

- **Removals are tracked**: uninstalling a plugin now shows on the **Plugin Updates** page and badges your avatar, just like an install, until the restart that applies it.
- **History of applied changes**: a collapsible **Previously applied** section lists what earlier restarts made live, grouped by restart. It keeps the last 50 changes and can be cleared.
- **Built for Jellyfin 12.0 and 12.1**: each release is now published once per server version, so the catalog offers a build that targets your server exactly.

## 🐞 Bug Fixes

- **One card per plugin**: installing and then updating a plugin before a restart shows as a single change, and installing then removing one shows nothing at all.
- **Manual task runs are safe**: running the plugin's startup task by hand from Scheduled Tasks no longer clears changes that are still waiting for a restart.
- **Sturdier saved state**: a damaged state file is kept aside as `updates.json.unreadable` instead of being overwritten, and one bad entry no longer costs the rest.

## 🐞 Bug Fixes

- **Nothing runs for non-admins**: the script checks who you are first, instead of every user's browser polling once a minute for an admin-only answer.
- **Far fewer checks**: every five minutes instead of every minute, and paused while the tab is in the background.
- **Smaller checks**: each check now asks only for the number it needs, instead of downloading every plugin's full release notes and throwing them away.
- **Switching tabs is free**: returning to the Jellyfin tab no longer triggers a fresh check.
- **Lighter on the browser**: the plugin now only keeps an eye on the page while a notification is actually showing, rather than constantly, for everyone.

## 📋 Notes

- The badge can now take up to five minutes to appear after a plugin is updated, rather than up to one. Opening the user menu always shows the current count.

## ✨ New Features

- **Plugin icon**: the plugin now has its own icon in the catalog and in your plugin list, instead of a blank placeholder.

## 🐞 Bug Fixes

- **Readable changelogs**: a plugin's release notes on the **Plugin Updates** page now appear properly formatted. Bold text, headings and links show as intended, instead of displaying the raw formatting characters around them.

## 📋 Notes

- Nothing to reconfigure. Updating takes only the usual restart.
- Still Jellyfin 12 only. The avatar badge and profile-menu entry need the [JavaScript Injector](https://github.com/n00bcodr/Jellyfin-JavaScript-Injector) plugin; the dashboard page works without it.

## Plugin Update Notifier 1.0.0.0

First release, for Jellyfin 12.

Jellyfin installs plugin updates in place but only applies them on the next server restart, and nothing in the UI tells an administrator that a restart is pending. This plugin closes that gap: it watches plugin install and update events and surfaces a clear, dismissible reminder until the server is restarted.

### Features

- Avatar badge: a dot appears on the admin's profile avatar the moment a plugin change leaves a restart pending.
- Profile-menu entry: a "Plugin Updates" item in the user dropdown, shown only to administrators, with a count of what changed.
- Dashboard page: lists every changed plugin, its old and new version, the release changelog, and a link to each plugin's source.
- Shared dismiss: dismissing hides the reminder for every admin session, not just one browser; a later plugin change brings it back.
- Self-clearing: the reminder disappears on its own after the restart it was asking for.

### Requirements

- Jellyfin 12 (this release uses APIs not present in 10.x).
- The avatar badge and profile-menu entry additionally require the [JavaScript Injector](https://github.com/n00bcodr/Jellyfin-JavaScript-Injector) plugin (4.0.0.0 or newer). The dashboard page works without it.

versions.changelog:
Scan efficiency overhaul. UI is unchanged.
- Sonarr per-series episode fetches now parallel (8 in flight). 100-show library ~8s sequential RTT -> ~1s.
- Jellyfin-mode Sonarr enrichment parallelized the same way.
- TMDB season fetches parallelized (4 in flight, well under TMDB's rate budget).
- ApplySonarrHasFile rewritten O(N*M) -> O(N). HashSet + List.RemoveAll instead of repeated List.Remove; seasons indexed once.
- ignoredTvdb HashSet hoisted out of per-series loop.
- JSON persistence switched to async I/O (WriteAllTextAsync).
Output is identical for identical input — pure internal refactor.

Editorial Revamp UI with Classic toggle.
- New Classic/Revamp segmented toggle in the hero. Old look stays exactly as it was; flip to Revamp for a full editorial overhaul (magazine spread, not dashboard). Preference saved per-browser.
- Revamp direction: ribbon hero with eyebrow + giant missing-count numeral hoisted via grid-template-areas, terminal-style `>` prompt search, vertical timeline scan history with circular dots, premiere-poster billboard cards (no chrome), chapter-numbered season heads via CSS counter, episode codes typeset as tracked-out mono eyebrows, settings card with mono uppercase labels.
- All Revamp rules scoped to #missingEpisodesPage[data-me-style=revamp] so the v1.0.8 Classic look is fully preserved.
- Fix: locked Search button tooltip on TMDB-detected episodes (Id=0) used to say 'Configure Sonarr to enable searching' even when Sonarr was configured. Tooltip now distinguishes 'Sonarr not configured' vs 'Not tracked by Sonarr'.

Final security pass + README refresh.
- Removed the /debug/parse diagnostic endpoint. Served its purpose chasing the Office/TMNT bug; no longer part of the public API surface.
- Dropped the FileScan log line from Information to Debug. Doesn't leak filesystem paths into the default Jellyfin logs anymore.
- README updated to document the three-layer accuracy model (Jellyfin / filename parse / Sonarr hasFile), pure-Jellyfin mode tradeoffs, and the full security posture.

- Accuracy: when 'Only monitored' is on, TMDB mode used to count every TMDB-listed episode as expected even if Sonarr had it unmonitored. Now drops unmonitored entries from the missing list during Sonarr enrichment, trimming 'phantom missing' episodes the user never wanted tracked.
- UI: the Jellyfin method explainer now mentions when Sonarr enrichment is active — surfaces the hasFile fallback so it's not invisible magic.

Fix scattered-folder case (TMNT-style): files exist on disk under Sonarr-managed per-season folders that neither Jellyfin's path nor Sonarr's series.Path cover. Enrichment now uses Sonarr's per-episode hasFile flag as ground truth — any missing entry Sonarr knows is already on disk gets dropped, season Have bumps, and series with everything now present fall out of the missing list automatically.

Actually fix the Office/TMNT accuracy bug.
- Root cause: when Jellyfin's cached series.Path was stale (points at an empty folder after files moved) and Sonarr tracked the correct path, my filename parser walked Jellyfin's empty path and returned 0 episodes. Enrichment later overwrote Size/Path with Sonarr's values but by then present/missing counts were already wrong.
- Fix: in Jellyfin-mode scans the plugin now pre-fetches Sonarr's series list (if configured), and when Jellyfin's path has 0 files/0 bytes it retries the parser against Sonarr's path for the same show (matched by TVDB id). The better result wins.
- Added a /debug/parse diagnostic endpoint + scan log line for future debugging.

Real accuracy fix.
- Rewrote ProcessJellyfinSeriesAsync around a clean present/expected separation. Filename-parsed episodes now correctly land in the present set without double-counting with TMDB's expected set.
- Previously: shows like The Office read as 0/186 even though the folder had 144GB of correctly-named S##E## files because filename merge was running AFTER partial stat accumulation and TMDB mode was then double-counting Total. Now stats are computed once, at the end, from |present| and |expected ∪ present|.
- Stale last-result.json from prior versions is naturally overwritten on the first 1.0.4 scan.

Accuracy fix + security hardening.
- Jellyfin scans now walk the series folder and parse S##E## / 1x05 patterns from filenames. Catches episodes that are on disk but Jellyfin's library never imported (was showing shows with 144 GB of files as 0/186).
- XSS hardening: image URLs for posters/backdrops/thumbnails now set via JS with JSON.stringify escaping instead of inline style interpolation — can't break out of the url() literal.
- Large internal refactor: the full Jellyfin scan now delegates per-series to the same helper the rescan-one button uses. No duplicated logic.
- README rewritten with AchievementBadges-style copy-paste install block and security section.

- Progress strip now shows during a single-show rescan (it was hidden because it lived inside the list-view container).
- Click an ignored show to open its detail view; dedicated 'Remove from ignore list' button replaces the old confirm prompt.
- README updated with new features and a note about the harmless 'error occurred while getting plugin details' warning for manually-installed copies.

- Per-show rescan no longer triggers a full library scan in Jellyfin mode (was doing a full scan and returning one entry).
- Rescan now uses Sonarr's tvdbId-indexed series lookup (one call instead of a full dump) and runs under the shared progress tracker, so the UI progress strip fills in during a rescan.
- Size chip moved inside the poster — no longer overlaps the meta row.
- Smarter path reconciliation: prefer Jellyfin's path when its folder has content, fall back to Sonarr when Jellyfin's path is stale / empty.

1.0 release.
- Jellyfin-only library size summing (no Sonarr required for the size chip).
- Clear-history button.
- Rescan single show from the detail view (no full rescan needed).
- Sort by size or by completion progress.
- Prefer Sonarr's series path when available — fixes stale Jellyfin paths.
- All prior 0.2 features.
First public beta.

versions.changelog:
✨ New Features

* Added Studio / Network, Decade, Hidden Gems and Finish These Collections sections, and enabled the previously developed Starring and Directed By sections (PR #292, @n00bcodr).
* Added per-section previews to the admin configuration page, allowing section results to be previewed before saving (PR #288, @n00bcodr).
* Added a new Add/Remove section workflow to make managing enabled sections easier (PR #288, @n00bcodr).

🛠️ Improvements

* Reworked section ordering in the admin configuration page with drag-and-drop support, including support for moving groups of sections that share the same order (PR #288, @n00bcodr).
* Added section information popovers using the new admin descriptions (PR #288, @n00bcodr).
* Improved section naming fallbacks and fixed missing Genre section localisation in the admin interface (PR #288, @n00bcodr).
* Escaped section metadata when rendering the home screen and settings interface so titles and names containing markup are displayed safely as text (PR #304, @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv).

🪲 Bug Fixes

* Fixed #297 where users on Jellyfin 12 could receive items from libraries they did not have access to in Latest Movies, Latest Shows, Recently Added and Genre sections (PR #301, @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv).
* Fixed #298 where authenticated users could access another user’s Home Screen Sections data by supplying that user’s ID. User-scoped endpoints are now bound to the authenticated user (PR #302, @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv).
* Fixed #298 by restricting section registration to administrators and limiting registered section result endpoints to the originating server (PR #303, @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv).

🌐 Translations

* Completed missing Spanish and Catalan translations (PR #293, @GospelBG).
* Added Greek translations (PR #299, @KaliDarkzy).

⚠️ Compatibility

* Added support for Jellyfin 12.2.
* Jellyfin 10.11.11 remains supported.

Contributors

* n00bcodr
* GospelBG
* KaliDarkzy
* 4eh5xitv6787h645ebv

versions.changelog: v0.9.0 - Grande passe de durcissement issue d'un 3e audit ultra-complet (10 dimensions, revue adversariale multi-agents) : 6 corrections MEDIUM + ~29 durcissements LOW, 0 critique/eleve restant. Recommandee. PAS DE MIGRATION. Compatible Jellyfin 10.11.10 et 10.11.11. MEDIUM : (1) coller un emoji au ras d'une limite de longueur pouvait faire echouer la sauvegarde de config (500 ; troncature UTF-16 rune-safe) ; (2) annuler l'avertissement 'utilisateurs en streaming' n'efface plus silencieusement les modifs de l'onglet Maintenance et n'affiche plus un faux succes ; (3) modales Uptime Kuma / Import accessibles (role=dialog, focus piege, Echap, focus restitue) ; (4) reordonnancement des lignes au clavier (fleches haut/bas) ; (5) la couche d'enforcement anti-SSRF des webhooks est desormais couverte par des tests ; (6) le pipeline de release verifie que l'URL d'asset du manifest correspond (anti-typo de casse type v0.6.0). LOW notables : anti lost-update entre onglets, purge des utilisateurs supprimes du suivi 'vu', tailles de boutons bornees, coherence de planning fixe C#/JS, ARIA onglets + navigation fleches, contrastes et cibles tactiles WCAG, garde double-execution du script injecte, un seul fetch /maintenance par navigation, test de reflexion des tiers d'autorisation, coherence de version sur 4 sources. + 2 liens de documentation corriges. 391 tests verts, build 0 warning.

v0.8.5 - Corrections UX/a11y/fonctionnel issues d'un 2e audit ultra-complet (toutes couches : UX, design, perf, code, a11y, docs ; 0 critique restant, 6 high corriges ici). Recommande. HIGH : (1) les modeles rapides d'annonce (ex : Halloween/Noel 'annuel') perdaient silencieusement leur planning / auto-expiration / theme / image -> l'annonce s'affichait toute l'annee au lieu de sa fenetre ; desormais tous les champs sont copies. (2) L'overlay de maintenance plein ecran a enfin la meme accessibilite que les modales d'annonce : role=dialog + aria-modal, focus piege a l'interieur, scroll de la page verrouille, focus restitue a la fermeture (avant : un utilisateur clavier/lecteur d'ecran pouvait tabuler derriere l'overlay). (3) En mode carousel, les cartes non visitees n'etaient jamais marquees 'vues' -> le carousel reapparaissait a chaque connexion ; maintenant toutes les cartes sont marquees a la fermeture. (4) Un redemarrage programme a la fin de la fenetre de maintenance etait annule silencieusement par la desactivation auto du meme tick -> il se declenche desormais correctement. (5) `make bump` (outil de dev) etait casse sur GNU sed (Git Bash / CI Linux). (6) README : exigence Jellyfin corrigee 10.11.6 -> 10.11.10. MEDIUM : cap sur le NOMBRE d'elements des collections (annonces 200 / messages 100 / etc.) anti-bloat config.xml ; image hero d'annonce masquee si l'URL est morte (plus d'icone cassee) ; pluralisation '1 annonce'. TESTS : 366/366 verts (+3 caps), build 0 warning, revue adversariale multi-agents (aucune regression critique/elevee). Compatible Jellyfin 10.11.10 et 10.11.11. PAS DE MIGRATION.

v0.8.4 - Release de SECURITE + corrections (suite a un audit adverse multi-agents). Recommande pour tous. SECURITE (webhook SSRF, durci sur 3 couches) : la defense SSRF de v0.7.0 etait contournable. Corrige : (1) le HttpClient webhook suivait les redirections HTTP -> un hote public autorise pouvait renvoyer un 302 vers 169.254.169.254 (metadata cloud) / loopback / LAN ; desormais AllowAutoRedirect=false + un ConnectCallback qui re-valide l'IP REELLE de chaque connexion (bat aussi le DNS rebinding). (2) les litteraux IPv6-mappes (::ffff:169.254.169.254) et les hotes a point final (127.0.0.1.) contournaient la blocklist -> normalisation MapToIPv4 + trailing-dot. (3) ajout des plages ::, CGNAT 100.64/10, fec0::/10, broadcast. NB : configurer un webhook reste admin-only (RequiresElevation), donc l'attaque exige un admin malveillant ou piege. CORRECTIONS (audit) : (a) la desactivation manuelle de la maintenance n'est plus annulee par le planificateur (consommation du ScheduledStart passe + garde ScheduledEnd) ; (b) ajouter un user a la whitelist PENDANT la maintenance le reactive immediatement, le drift-check respecte la whitelist live ; (c) modele de concurrence APPLIQUE : tous les writers de config (SaveConfig/SaveMaintenance/SaveAdminAnnouncements/MarkSeen/ResetSeen + tache planifiee) passent par un verrou unique -> fin des pertes d'ecriture et du config.xml corrompu ; (d) les annonces recurrentes (daily/weekly/annual) sont evaluees en heure LOCALE serveur (etait UTC) -> elles s'affichent aux bonnes heures, alignees sur les bannieres (positionne le TZ du conteneur) ; (e) cap sur la taille de reponse webhook (anti-OOM) + try/catch global sur la tache planifiee ; (f) admin.js : fix d'une fuite de listeners (double-binding a chaque pageshow). CI : la garde ASCII attrape desormais U+2028/2029/0085 ; release.yml lance dotnet test avant de publier ; creation de release idempotente. TESTS : 363/363 verts (etait 316), correctifs SSRF mutation-verifies, revue adversariale multi-agents (aucune regression critique/elevee). PAS DE MIGRATION.

v0.8.3 - Release de durcissement qualite (reponse a un audit adverse). AUCUN changement de feature, AUCUN changement de comportement du plugin shippe : le DLL est fonctionnellement identique a v0.8.2. La seule modif du code shippe est un refactor interne behavior-preserving (extraction de MaintenanceHelper.SetUserDisabledAsync, la glue IUserManager.GetUserDto+UpdatePolicyAsync, factorisee depuis les 3 boucles activate/deactivate/drift-check) verifie equivalent par mutation testing. Tout le reste est de l'infra de test/CI qui ne part PAS dans le zip : (1) Garde anti-tests-vacuous via Stryker.NET (mutation testing) sur les helpers de logique pure (AnnouncementHelper + MaintenanceHelper), workflow dedie manuel+hebdo, seuil de non-regression. (2) +21 tests xUnit (295 -> 316) : durcissement HasUserSeen/MarkSeen, round-trip XML de PluginConfiguration (compat legacy + champs non-null), builders de payload webhook Discord/Slack/Generic, vecteurs XSS sur SAFE_URL_RE, et surtout 15 tests d'integration HTTP qui pilotent SaveConfig/SaveMaintenance/SaveAdminAnnouncements a travers un VRAI Plugin (BasePlugin sur dossier temp + XmlSerializer reel) avec preuve de persistance disque. (3) Smoke test de deploiement reel qui gate les releases : boot d'un vrai serveur Jellyfin (matrix 10.11.6 plancher targetAbi + 10.11.10 prod) avec le DLL monte, completion du wizard, auth admin, puis appel de /users-summary et /announcements/admin (les endpoints qui appellent IUserManager.GetUsers() - EXACTEMENT la methode qui crashait en MissingMethodException sur 10.11.9) + scan des logs serveur. Ce gate aurait attrape le bug v0.8.0 avant publication. TESTS : 316/316 verts sur SDK 10.11.10, refactor mutation-verifie (24/24 + nouveaux KILLED). PAS DE MIGRATION. Recommande pour 10.11.10+ ; equivalent fonctionnel a v0.8.2.

v0.8.2 - Compat refresh Jellyfin 10.11.10. Aucun changement de code, aucun changement de feature : juste un rebuild contre le SDK Jellyfin 10.11.10 (release patch sortie cote serveur) + bump targetAbi de 10.11.9.0 a 10.11.10.0 pour que Jellyfin 10.11.10+ accepte l'install sans warning. AUDIT API : diff complet de IUserManager + ISessionManager entre 10.11.9 et 10.11.10 = 0 difference, toutes les methodes utilisees (GetUsers, GetUserById, GetUserByName, GetUserDto, UpdatePolicyAsync, Sessions) ont signature identique. v0.8.1 (build 10.11.9) marche aussi sur 10.11.10 grace a la forward-compat Jellyfin meme-minor, mais ce binaire v0.8.2 est strictement aligne sur la derniere API. TESTS : 279/279 verts sur SDK 10.11.10. PAS DE MIGRATION. Si tu es sur Jellyfin <= 10.11.8, reste sur v0.8.0. Si tu es sur 10.11.9, v0.8.1 ou v0.8.2 marchent les deux. Si tu es sur 10.11.10+, v0.8.2 recommande.

v0.8.1 - HOTFIX CRITIQUE Jellyfin 10.11.9 : la propriete IUserManager.Users a ete supprimee dans Jellyfin 10.11.x (breaking change patch) au profit de la methode GetUsers(). Le plugin v0.8.0 (build contre SDK 10.11.6) crashait avec MissingMethodException 'Method not found: ... IUserManager.get_Users()' sur les routes /MaintenanceDeluxe/users-summary, /MaintenanceDeluxe/announcements/admin, et lors de l'activation maintenance (MaintenanceHelper.ActivateAsync). Pire : les exceptions remontaient dans les handlers ItemAdded/Updated/Removed de Jellyfin (via la stack DI partagee), cassant des fonctionnalites core du serveur. Fix : (1) bump Jellyfin.Controller + Jellyfin.Model de 10.11.6 -> 10.11.9 (csproj plugin ET csproj tests). (2) Remplacement de _userManager.Users par _userManager.GetUsers() sur 3 call sites : BannerController.GetUsersSummary (ligne 549), BannerController.GetAdminAnnouncements (ligne 704), MaintenanceHelper.ActivateAsync (ligne 138). (3) targetAbi du manifest passe de 10.11.6.0 a 10.11.9.0 - les serveurs Jellyfin sur 10.11.6/7/8 ne pourront plus installer v0.8.1+ via le manifest (downgrade SDK pas backward-compatible). Si tu es sur 10.11.6-8, reste sur v0.8.0 ou upgrade Jellyfin. TESTS : 279/279 verts sur le nouveau SDK 10.11.9 (aucune logique modifiee, juste l'API de IUserManager). PAS D'AUTRE CHANGEMENT cote feature - c'est strictement un hotfix de compat ABI.

v0.8.0 - Tour de fixes a11y + UX + CI robustesse (4 agents en parallele, +13 tests = 279 verts). A11Y: (1) Focus trap dans toutes les modales (dangerConfirm admin + showAnnouncementModal + Carousel + Stack banner.js) - Tab/Shift+Tab cycle dans la modale, capture/restore du document.activeElement. (2) Scroll lock body lors d'affichage modale annonce (overflow:hidden sur documentElement+body, restore au close). (3) Compteur carousel SR-friendly - counterEl cree une fois hors render() avec aria-atomic=true, mutation via textContent au lieu d'innerHTML wipe. (4) prefers-reduced-motion respecte (theme neon pulse, badge dirty pulse, jfDconfFade overlay animation, preview neon glow). (5) Contraste WCAG AA sur badges - draft #E8A33D->#FFD27A + opacity 0.18->0.28, expired #D9534F->#FF8A87 + opacity 0.15->0.30, expiring + schedule-incomplete aussi rehausses. (6) Touch targets 44x44 minimum sur .jf-dconf-btn (padding 8->12) et .jf-url-btn (padding 7->12 + min-height 44 + inline-flex). (7) Focus visible outline doree sur les inputs .jf-ann-field. (8) backdrop-filter fallback solide via @supports not (backdrop-filter) - fallback opaque pour vieux Chromium TV. UX: (9) Webhook test button desactive pendant la requete avec texte 'Test en cours...', reenable() partage entre then/catch. (10) Import config: _pendingImport=null sur Cancel/ESC/backdrop, garde Apply qui affiche feedback si pas de fichier selectionne, closeImportModal() centralise. (11) Release notes delete confirmation via dangerConfirm si la section a du contenu (titre/body/icon non vides), delete direct sinon. (12) Draft autosave: console.warn one-shot via _draftSaveFailed flag si quota localStorage depasse. (13) configPage.html: datetime-local placeholder='YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM' + pattern regex pour vieux Safari mobile sans support natif. INFRA: (14) escape_non_ascii.py utilise encoding='utf-8-sig' (strippe BOM auto). (15) check_version_coherence.py try/except sur parsing JSON/XML malformes -> exit 2 avec message clair. (16) WebhookNotifier SanitiseExceptionMessage + TryGetRetryAfterSeconds passees private->internal pour tests directs. TESTS: 13 nouveaux cas xUnit (SanitiseExceptionMessage 7 cas redaction URL+host, TryGetRetryAfterSeconds 4 cas null/cap60s/delta/pastdate, IsTargetedAtUser_DraftWithRoleAndUuidFilters regression guard, IsScheduleActive_Daily_MidnightWrap_ExactBoundaries). 266 v0.7.0 -> 279 v0.8.0. PAS DE MIGRATION : aucun nouveau champ, fixes defensifs uniquement.

v0.7.0 - Audit secondaire : 11 fixes (3 securite + 4 robustesse + 4 polish), 32 nouveaux tests xUnit (234 -> 266). (1) CRITIQUE banner.js checkTimeWindow overnight wrap : les banniers/annonces avec fenetre daily 22:00-06:00 retournaient toujours false, donc invisibles la nuit alors que le C# MatchesTimeWindow gerait correctement le wrap. Divergence client/serveur corrigee. (2) SSRF defense webhook URL : nouvelle helper IsWebhookHostSafe qui rejette loopback IPv4/IPv6 (127.0.0.0/8, ::1), link-local 169.254.0.0/16 (incl. AWS/Azure/GCP metadata endpoints), RFC1918 prive (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16), IPv6 ULA fc00::/7, hostnames .localhost/.internal/.local, et localhost literal. Appliquee sur SaveMaintenance webhook URL ET TestWebhook endpoint. (3) WebhookNotifier log sanitization : SanitiseExceptionMessage strippe les URLs+tokens du message exception avant logging (LogWarning ne contient plus la URL discord avec son token). TestAsync retourne message generique a l'admin UI au lieu de ex.Message qui pouvait leak hostnames internes via SSL cert errors. (4) Init defensif Announcements + AnnouncementsSeen avec = new() property-level (en plus du constructeur) : XmlSerializer peut bypasser le constructeur sur XML legacy nil tags, laissant ces props null et causant NRE. (5) ValidateSchedules WeekDays empty/null : au lieu de rejeter (regression v0.6.1), auto-normaliser type='always'. Preserve la compat avec configs legacy qui avaient ce cas comme 'never-active' silencieux. (6) DetectFormat URL host parsing au lieu de substring match : avant, 'https://relay.com/discord-bot/api/webhooks/proxy' etait classifie Discord (faux positif). Maintenant utilise Uri.Host exact match (incl. canary.discord.com, ptb.discord.com). (7) GetActiveSessions snapshot ToList avant LINQ : evite race condition sur _sessionManager.Sessions collection mutable. (8) ClonePublicFields rendu internal + reutilise par MaintenanceScheduleTask au lieu de son snapshot field-by-field qui manquait ScheduledStart/End/ActivatedAt. (9) WebhookNotifier 429 Retry-After : respecte le header (en seconds ou HTTP-date), retry si <= 4s d'attente. (10) Webhook payload size cap 32KB : evite Discord/Slack/proxy 400 sur payloads trop gros (admin avec customTitle+customSubtitle+message tres longs). (11) banner.js tick() defensive null check sur CONFIG : si fetch /config fail (plugin disabled mid-session, network blip), CONFIG reste null et chaque CONFIG.* etait NRE. (12) LastModified monotone : Math.Max(old, now) protege contre les horloges qui reculent (NTP correction). TESTS : 32 nouveaux (15 cas checkTimeWindow overnight JS, 7 SSRF blocklist hosts, 6 boundary public ranges, 5 DetectFormat regression guards substring-match, ValidateSchedules WeekDays auto-correct 2 cas, NormaliseCssColor bounds revisited). 234 -> 266 verts.

v0.6.1 - Hotfix install + audit logique. (1) CRITIQUE: fix sourceUrl lowercase typo qui cassait l'installation Jellyfin de v0.6.0 (GitHub URLs case-sensitive, 'maintenance-deluxe' lowercase -> 404). (2) AUDIT FIXES: 7 trous logiques cibles par l'audit pre-v0.6.1. (a) CSS .theme-custom ajoutee a admin.css avec vars CSS dynamiques pour preview admin du theme personnalise (avant : preview affichait velours par defaut, le theme custom n'etait visible que sur le client final). (b) ValidateSchedules etendu : valide les bornes coherence interne sur les 3 types : 'fixed' rejette FixedStart >= FixedEnd, 'annual' rejette mois hors [1,12] ou jour hors [1,31], 'weekly' rejette weekDays empty ou jours hors [0,6]. Avant : admin pouvait save des schedules muets qui ne matchaient jamais. (c) PLUGIN_VERSION constante au top d'admin.js (etait hardcodee '0.3.2.0' depuis 7 versions). (d) Sélecteur 'Personnalisé' disable + opacity 0.4 + tooltip explicatif tant que customTheme=null, avec auto-fallback velours si l'admin avait setce le theme custom puis supprime sa config. (e) Badge schedule incomplet en rouge dashed ('Fenetre fixe non configuree', 'Annuel non configure', 'Hebdo (aucun jour)') au lieu du badge bleu trompeur. (f) expireAfterDays clamp client-side 1-365 avec mise a jour de l'input (plus de surprise quand le serveur reduit a 365). (g) NormaliseCssColor : case-insensitive sur rgba (RGBA(...) accepte) + validation bounds R/G/B in [0,255] (avant : rgb(256,0,0) accepte produisait du CSS invalide silencieux). (3) REFACTOR: SAFE_URL_RE constante module-level dans banner.js, remplace 4 regex dupliques identiques (XSS protocol-relative defense). (4) UX: 2 nouveaux ANN_TEMPLATES quick-add 'Soiree Halloween' (schedule annual Oct 25-Nov 1) et 'Fin d'annee' (schedule annual Dec 20-Jan 5 wrap), template 'Nouveaux films' expireAfterDays=14 prefilled. (5) DOCS: docs/announcements.md mis a jour avec tableau Phase 2 features (carousel/stack/draft/expire/schedule/image/viewport/custom theme), tableau complet des 19 champs Announcement avec types et defaults, 'truth matrix' AND-combined des filtres de livraison, projection serveur de /announcements/active expliquee. (6) TESTS xUnit : 21 nouveaux cas. ValidateSchedules Theory (fixed inverted, fixed open-ended, annual out-of-range 6 cas, annual wrap valide, weekly empty, weekly null, weekly out-of-range 3 cas, daily no-constraint), NormaliseCssColor Theory (RGBA case-insensitive 2, rgb out-of-range 3, boundary 1). 213 tests v0.6.0 -> 234 tests v0.6.1. PAS DE MIGRATION : aucun champ ajoute, fixes defensifs uniquement.

v0.6.0 - Phase 2 annonces complete : editeur de theme custom. Tu peux maintenant creer ton propre theme d'annonce avec ta palette / police / bordure preferes, sans toucher au code.
